Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pod5r 0.2.0 (development)

Bug fixes

  • Heap memory is no longer overwritten when pore types and end reasons are read. The pinned POD5 C API (c0be435) writes the string terminator one byte past the size it reports in pod5_get_pore_type() and pod5_get_end_reason(). The native reader now allocates one additional byte for both buffers. The issue affected every metadata request through read_pod5(), extract_pod5_signal(), process_pod5(), and extract_pod5_signal_dorado(). Returned values are unchanged, but the overflow could corrupt memory and cause unpredictable crashes on other data or systems.

pod5r 0.1.0 (development)

Native POD5 reading

  • extract_pod5_signal_dorado() maps Dorado simplex child UUIDs through explicit pi, sp, ts, and ns tags to parent POD5 signal intervals. It preserves separate children and rejects missing or out-of-range coordinates.

  • Missing floating-point metadata is normalised to NA_real_ at the R boundary. Historical v0 event counts remain upstream migration defaults; see read_pod5().

  • Read-count limits are checked before selection and output allocations.

  • Duplicate file UUIDs have regression coverage and documented selection semantics.

  • Native linkage explicitly includes zlib. Fixture generation uses named member assignments to make changes to upstream structs easier to review.

  • read_pod5() retrieves read metadata and optional signals through the native POD5 C API, without Python or reticulate.

  • extract_pod5_signal() supports indexed UUID selection, exact raw counts, picoampere calibration, and chunk-aware sample intervals.

  • process_pod5() processes consecutive read groups without retaining callback results, supporting incremental workflows on larger files.

  • read_pod5_runs() exposes run metadata, context tags, and tracking dictionaries.

  • Mixed-run readers initialise the upstream run cache in file-index order, preventing duplicate run records after acquisition-ID lookups.
